lead: GameStop / GME — the bitcoin pivot the crowd now questions
smaller: Oklo / OKLO — is the regulator the real risk?
Eli Lilly / LLY — the leveraged fund is a click away
Nasdaq 100 / QQQ — everyday investors buy the tariff dip
why_lead: The largest one-session move among the retail names in the market card (GameStop down 22.11% in the prior session) is a changed story, not a repeat of the 27 March lead: the break that lead named at the 24.48 reference has now been reached, and the new facts are the convertible-bond financing, the store closures and investors questioning the pivot. Tesla was the alternative, but its angle is the same Musk-comeback catalyst that the 25 and 26 March editions already used.
why_smaller: Oklo is a changed story, not the 27 March meltdown-buy angle again: the NRC rejection and return, the 75MW capacity news and a printed bear case are new, and the price fell another 9.67% in the prior session.

Eli Lilly is the non-AI, non-meme slot: single-stock leveraged and inverse funds debuted on 26 March and Thailand opened leveraged ETF sales to retail, while the 21 March TQQQ smaller was about inflows into an existing fund.

Nasdaq 100 / QQQ is a retail-flow story with a new observation: Business Insider's near-record dip buying, with a tariff catalyst and the VIX down from 21.13 to 18.69; it is not the TQQQ inflow story the 21 March smaller already told.
considered_not_chosen: Tesla: lead slots on 12, 17, 24 and 25 March and a smaller on 26 March all carry the Musk-comeback or tariff-leeway catalyst; the 27 March auto-tariff and meme-label headlines are a second read on the same tariff story, so a fifth Tesla slot in four days would repeat the angle.

Silver: the 7 March smaller already told the squeeze story; SLV closed at 31.32 and the Kitco, Livemint and Sprott headlines are flow colour on the same call. The draft's break (a close back under 31.80) was also wrong, because SLV is already below 31.80 and 31.80 is the spot-silver reference.
D-Wave / QBTS: quantum lead slots on 19 and 21 March, a smaller on 14 March and the 'next AI' hook from 12 and 13 March; the only change is price.
Nebius: a Reddit AI-pick headline and a -20.72% 20-session move, but no concrete catalyst today and an AI-infrastructure overlap with Oklo.
Robinhood: the bank and cash-delivery launch was the 27 March smaller trade.
Dogecoin: four earlier smaller slots; the Musk meme headline does not change the meme-coin story.
Nvidia: the May 15 date and the keynote and roadmap angles were the 18 and 20 March smaller trades.
Rivian: a 19.67% five-session move with a single stock-chart headline on spin-off excitement, too thin for an essay.
U.S. Steel, Tenon Medical, SurgePays, Trimble and XTIA: retail-attention headlines exist, but the tickers are not in the market card, so no price evidence can be cited.
Gold / GLD: smaller slots on 17, 19 and 24 March already covered the record and the reserve-to-bitcoin headlines, and the 26 March reserve-sale item repeats that angle.
